challenges.name: progress-service-quiz
challenges.title: Monotonic progress and one event per real change
challenges.description: Two pieces of evidence from the progress service: a late update from an old tab that lowered a finished lesson, and a leaderboard that counted one lesson completion three times.

questions.question:
The progress handler stores a lesson percent with:

UPDATE lesson_progress SET percent = $3, updated_at = now()
WHERE user_id = $1 AND lesson_id = $2;

API log for one learner (laptop tab and an old phone tab):
09:14:02.118 PATCH /progress lesson=sql-3 percent=100 -> 200 (laptop)
09:14:02.904 PATCH /progress lesson=sql-3 percent=60  -> 200 (phone, sent at 09:13:40, retried after a network drop)

SELECT percent FROM lesson_progress WHERE user_id = 'u_an' AND lesson_id = 'sql-3';  -> 60

Statement: "Changing the assignment to SET percent = GREATEST(percent, $3) keeps the stored value at 100 when the 60 arrives after the 100, without any lock taken by the application."
questions.explanation: True. GREATEST(percent, $3) reads the current value and computes the new one inside the same UPDATE, and PostgreSQL holds the row lock for the duration of that statement, so the late 60 cannot overwrite the 100: GREATEST(100, 60) = 100. That is exactly the monotonic rule (a lesson percent never goes down) expressed as one atomic statement. The common misconception is that you need to order requests by a client timestamp to fix this; client clocks and retries make timestamps unreliable, while "never lower it" needs no clock at all. To know whether to publish an event, add RETURNING and compare with the old value (or use WHERE percent < $3 and check the row count).

False. Deduplication by eventId catches the same event delivered twice (a redelivery). These are three different events with three different ids, created by three requests, so the consumer correctly treats them as three facts and adds the completion points three times. The fix is at the producer: publish only when the write really changed the document (here the version stayed 7, so nothing changed after the first write). The misconception is that consumer-side idempotency can repair a producer that invents duplicate facts; it only removes duplicate deliveries of one fact.

challenges.name: progress-service-apply-update
challenges.title: Validate and apply progress updates
challenges.description:
Write applyProgress(update, catalog, store, bus), the core of the CodeDev progress service. Every PATCH /progress request becomes one call; the runner applies the updates in order and prints one line per update, the published events and the stored documents.

Input (untrusted): update = { userId, courseId, lessonId, percent }, where percent can be any JSON value. The catalog gives catalog.courses[courseId] = { lessons: string[], required?: { [lessonId]: challengeIds[] } }, catalog.enrollments[userId] = course ids and catalog.passed[userId] = challenge ids the learner has passed (missing entries mean empty lists).

Checks, in this order; the first failing one decides the result { status: "rejected", error }:
1. percent is a JSON number that is an integer from 0 to 100, else INVALID_PERCENT ("60", null, true, 99.9, -1, 101 and a missing percent are all invalid).
2. courseId is a course of the catalog, else UNKNOWN_COURSE.
3. lessonId is one of that course's lessons, else LESSON_NOT_IN_COURSE.
4. the learner is enrolled in the course, else NOT_ENROLLED.
5. percent 100 (completing the lesson) only when every required challenge of that lesson is in catalog.passed[userId], else CHALLENGES_NOT_PASSED. Lower percents need no challenge.

Then, with the learner's document from store.get(userId, courseId) ({ version, lessons, coursePercent }; version 0 and no lessons when new):
- Monotonic: if percent is not above the stored percent of that lesson (a missing lesson counts as 0), return { status: "unchanged", lessonPercent: <stored percent> } without writing anything or publishing anything.
- Otherwise set the lesson percent, set coursePercent = Math.floor(sum of the percents of ALL lessons of the course, missing ones as 0, divided by the number of lessons), add 1 to version, store the document with store.put, publish exactly one event { type: "progress.updated", userId, courseId, lessonId, lessonPercent, coursePercent, version } with the new values, and return { status: "applied", lessonPercent, coursePercent, version }.

Each (learner, course) has its own document and version. Do not change the types, ProgressStore, EventBus or the test runner. The output must be deterministic: same input, same lines.
hints: Which of these updates may change the stored document: a valid 60 after a stored 80, a valid 80 after a stored 80, a valid 81 after a stored 80? Only one of them may publish an event.

Write the five checks first, each returning early, in the order the description lists them. Then compare the new percent with doc.lessons[lessonId] ?? 0, and compute the course percent from course.lessons (every lesson of the course), not from the lessons the learner has started.

A similar rule on different data: a course with lessons [a, b, c, d, e] and a stored document { a: 100, c: 30 } has course percent Math.floor((100 + 0 + 30 + 0 + 0) / 5) = 26. A new update c = 30 leaves it unchanged (no event), while c = 45 gives Math.floor(145 / 5) = 29 and version + 1.
